headline: OpenAI launches 'dots' as an always-on personal AI assistant, evolved from coding tools
summary: Available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers and higher, 'dots' integrates with your calendar and email to proactively assist with tasks, aiming for ubiquity.
details: OpenAI has launched "dots," an always-on AI personal assistant designed to work proactively in the background. It is available to ChatGPT desktop and mobile app subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. 'dots' connects to your calendar, email, and computer tools to help manage tasks.

The assistant evolved from OpenAI's Codex coding tools, which offered similar functionality but required more manual input. The shift aimed to repackage this technology into something more accessible and intuitive for general users. This aligns with a broader trend of AI companies developing persistent, proactive assistants.

Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, explained that framing 'dots' as a single, continuous conversation entity makes it more intuitive. The name itself, a play on the negative space in OpenAI's logo, is intended to convey ubiquity. This approach aims for a user experience where the assistant "feels" like it's thinking about you.

'dots' is designed to anticipate needs without constant prompting, leading to increased token usage for OpenAI and a more proactive experience for users. Early testing shows it can flag calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines. While timing is expected to improve, the ability to analyze and provide useful information during an outage has already proven valuable.

The assistant employs "proactive research," where it considers what it knows about you, past conversations, and granted access to propose helpful actions. This raises questions about the balance between the AI model's data needs for usefulness and the extent of personal data exposure to the software company.

headline_marked: [[Instagram testing 90-minute horizontal video]] format, taking on YouTube
headline: Instagram testing 90-minute horizontal video format, taking on YouTube
summary: Instagram is reportedly testing a new long-form horizontal video format, allowing videos up to 90 minutes. This move positions the platform to directly compete with YouTube, starting with select creators in the U.S.
details: According to The Hollywood Reporter, Instagram has begun testing a new long-form horizontal video format. This trial is currently underway with select creators in the U.S., allowing videos up to 90 minutes in length.

This marks a significant strategic shift for Instagram, which has primarily focused on short-form vertical video content like Reels. The move directly positions the platform to compete with YouTube's dominance in long-form video.

The extended duration could open up new possibilities for creators, enabling them to produce more in-depth content, documentaries, or episodic series. It also suggests Instagram is exploring ways to expand its viewing experience beyond mobile devices.

The initiative aims to attract a broader range of content and creators, potentially increasing user engagement and time spent on the platform. This could also pave the way for new monetization opportunities for creators and Instagram itself.
